subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should the shipped `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` contract become fail-closed above 1 MiB, and is that the canonical limit for memory-wiki synthesis bodies?
rationale: Source inspection can validate the bounded reader, but only the memory-wiki owner can decide whether breaking previously accepted large files and choosing this threshold is intentional product policy.

options.title: Define a canonical limit
options.body: Choose the supported maximum and affected input surfaces, then align implementation, tests, docs, upgrade guidance, and real CLI proof to that contract.

options.title: Keep current compatibility
options.body: Retain unlimited body-file acceptance until a concrete downstream maximum or observed resource failure justifies a breaking limit.

options.title: Accept 1 MiB now
options.body: Own the compatibility break explicitly and require release context plus fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Define a canonical limit
recommendation.body: Choose the supported maximum and affected input surfaces, then align implementation, tests, docs, upgrade guidance, and real CLI proof to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available recent history signal for memory-wiki runtime and CLI behavior.
